html:
SMTO-BOOT-0051 — SMTO couldn't load its security certificate

GUID: 3303fe91-70ca-4053-8560-eb6bd554ed1c
Slug: startup-tls-setup-failed
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: startup

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't use the certificate that gives it a secure https:// address. When started normally, it may come back on a plain http:// address until this is fixed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If SMTO opens at an address starting with http://, sign in and open Settings › Security › HTTPS & Certificates. SMTO falls back to an unencrypted address when its certificate fails, so you can still reach this page.
  2. Choose Upload an existing certificate and add the certificate with its matching private key, or choose Generate a local HTTPS certificate, then apply it. The certificate and key must belong together, and the key can't be password-protected.
  3. If SMTO doesn't open at all, ask the person who manages SMTO to check the certificate and key files it starts with. Only someone with access to the server's files can fix them when SMTO can't open.

What success looks like

  • SMTO opens at its https:// address, and Settings › Security › HTTPS & Certificates shows the current certificate.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Never send the private key file itself, and don't turn off certificate checks to get past this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Server's HTTPS listener could not create its TLS context because the configured certificate or private key could not be loaded (unreadable, unsupported format, encrypted key, or not a matching pair).

What this means

  • The HTTP server could not initialize its TLS context before accepting connections. The certificate and private key must be readable, valid for their intended use, and form a matching pair. This does not diagnose a model provider certificate.

Why this can happen

  • A TLS context can reject malformed certificates, unreadable private keys, incompatible key material, or a certificate/key mismatch.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the failed HTTPS startup stage and the certificate tooling on the controller host; do not paste the private key into diagnostics.

How to fix it

  • Check the certificate and key the listener uses (the certificate store in the state directory's .tls folder, or --ssl-certfile/--ssl-keyfile and AOR_SSL_CERTFILE/AOR_SSL_KEYFILE, default artifacts/ssl/agent-ui.crt and agent-ui.key): both must be readable by the service account and PEM-encoded, the key unencrypted, and the public key from openssl x509 -noout -pubkey must match openssl pkey -pubout for the key. Install a matching pair through Settings › Security › HTTPS & Certificates or replace the files, then restart; under the web bundle a failing certificate makes the listeners restart over HTTP.
  • SMTO administrator: verify the configured certificate and key files, their access permissions, supported format, and matching public keys. Restore the intended matching pair and restart the controller.

Retry and execution caution

  • Restart after repairing the controller HTTPS identity.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended HTTPS address accepts connections with the configured certificate.

What not to do

  • Do not replay completed work or weaken authentication and certificate checks to clear this diagnostic.

Technical notes

  • Keep TLS verification enabled. The operating system must allow the service account to read its key.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
